texts.preamble: Rakeshkumar C.T vs Shafiulla on 20 June, 2025 Kabc020183752023 Before Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru City Scch-17 Present: Sri.KANCHI Mayanna Goutam B.A.L, Ll.M., Member, Mact Xix Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru.
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act by claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 30-09-2022. 2. The petition averments in brief are as under: On 30-09-2024 at about 2.00 a.m.,the petitioner was traveling in Tata AC Sleeper coach Bus bearing No.KA-59-9666 from Bengaluru to Chennai NH road, while bus reached near Nekkundhi village, at that time the driver of the Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing No.KA-53- 2458 has parked the lorry on the road without any indicator or signal and without keeping any safety cone beside the lorry had parked on the road negligently, meanwhile the driver of the bus hit the lorry from behind, and caused the accident. As a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government hospital, Vaniyambadi wherein first aid treatment was given, thereafter petitioner was shifted to Atreum Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he took treatment and underwent surgery. Petitioner has spent a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges. Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy, aged about 27 years and working as Software Engineer at Excelencia iTech Consulting and earning Rs.1,00,000/- per month. Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to do his work as he was doing prior to the said accident and suffered loss of income. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest. 3. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1- owner has not appeared before the tribunal, hence placed exparte. After service of notice, the respondent No.2-insurer appeared through its counsel. Respondent No.2 - insurance company has filed its written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the Lorry bearing No. KA.53-2458 and the liability of this respondent is any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and the policy was valid at the time of accident. It has specifically submitted that the petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties to the proceedings i.e., the owner and insurer of the Bus bearing No.KA-59-9666 not made as party to the proceedings. Hence it is required to direct the claimant to implead the same as party to the proceedings in order to adjudicate the matter factually and effectually. Further it has denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. Further it has contended that, the respondent No.1 owner has entrusted the vehicle to the person who was not having valid driving license and the vehicle was not having Rakeshkumar C.T vs Shafiulla on 20 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164902602/ 2 valid permit and fitness as on the time of accident and hence violated the policy conditions . It has further denied the cause and manner of accident. Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act. Accordingly prays to dismiss the claim petition against it. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 21. Further, examined the Orthopedic Doctor at Atreum Hospital, Bengaluru and Dr. Nagaraj B N, Orthopaedic surgeon at SOADS hospital as PW.2 and 3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.22 & 23. 6. In continuation of Ex.P1, the IO prepared IMV reports of both the vehicles involved in the accident which are marked as Ex.P2 and 3 shows that offending Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing No.KA-53-2458 has got damages i.e., left side and rear load body broken, left side rear chassis frame, rear cross bar bent, both tail lamps broken, left side rear stepny bracket damaged and the Bus bearing No.KA-59-9666 has got damaged to right side front body torn out and pressed inward upto right side 1st window, both lower and upper berth damaged, right side front window glass broken, right side driver seat, steering assembly, dash board broken and pressed inward, right side air filter broken, front bumper broken, right side front cross bar bent, front wind sheild glass broken, right side front head light indicator broken, right side top body torn out, front right side body show set broken, right side front wheel cover broken, right side front tie rod bent, right side front platform bent, right side rear view mirror broken, right side EC board assembly broken, right side front wirings damaged, right side driver door pressed inward.
texts.arguments: The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus: "12. At this juncture, I would like to quote the following judgment wherein it states that; 2009 ACJ 287 ( National Ins. Co. V/s. Pushparama and others), wherein it is held that, Certified copy of the criminal court records such as FIR, recovery and mechanical inspection of the vehicle or documents are of sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the rider was negligent. 13. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants. In the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka 1449-2023 connected with 3330-2023 between Iffco Tokio Gen. Ins. Co. ltd., V/s. Smt. Jayashree and another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that when there is no exact evidence to show that due to the injuries the petitioner has lost working capacity, the consideration of loss of future income due to disability does not arise. The learned counsel for respondent No.2-insurance company relied on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in ILR 2010 KAR 2439 in between Sri.Subash V/s The New India Assurance Company Ltd., Represented by its Manager and Others wherein held that, "If the claimant is continued in service, then, the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise." As the petitioner continued with service and he has not suffered any financial loss. No evidence is also placed by showing that he has not received any salary during the laid up period. Hence, the petitioner is not entitle for compensation under these head.
texts.respondent_arguments: The learned counsel for respondent No.2-insurance company relied on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in ILR 2010 KAR 2439 in between Sri.Subash V/s The New India Assurance Company Ltd., Represented by its Manager and Others wherein held that, "If the claimant is continued in service, then, the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise." As the petitioner continued with service and he has not suffered any financial loss. No evidence is also placed by showing that he has not received any salary during the laid up period. Hence, the petitioner is not entitle for compensation under these head.
